title: Jyotika Calls Suriya an 'Absolute Green Flag' as Couple Nears 20th Wedding Anniversary
excerpt: In a candid interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, actress Jyotika praised her husband Suriya's deep belief in equality, revealing she once earned three times his salary and calling him remarkable 'as a man, as a husband, and as an actor.'
body:
• Jyotika called Suriya an "absolute green flag," praising his commitment to equality and shared responsibilities in their nearly 20-year marriage.
  • The actress revealed she once earned three times Suriya's salary during their early careers, joking it is now "30 times less."
  • Suriya credited Jyotika's trust and support during the financial challenges of producing his blockbuster film Karuppu.
  • The couple, who married in September 2006, have not acted together in a film since their wedding despite being one of Tamil cinema's most beloved on-screen pairs.

Jyotika Praises Suriya's Belief in Equality

Actress Jyotika has described her husband, Tamil cinema star Suriya, as a "green flag" in a wide-ranging interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, published ahead of their 20th wedding anniversary in September.

Speaking about the foundation of their marriage, Jyotika said Suriya's commitment to equality has been unwavering from the start. "He's remarkable as a man, as a husband, and as an actor, of course. There is an equality in his head, and I feel you have to be born with that. It has to be an inner feel. Otherwise, it doesn't reflect," she said, according to The Hollywood Reporter India.

The actress elaborated on how responsibilities at home are divided equally. "You have to feel the woman with you. If she doesn't want to cook, let it be. I am not trying to be a feminist here. But we are equals at home. And it only comes out of a genuine, deep within feeling inside a man. Suriya has it in him," she said, as reported by The Times of Bengal.

The Salary Revelation That Made Headlines

In one of the interview's most discussed moments, Jyotika revealed that early in their careers, she was paid three times more than Suriya. "At that time, I was paid three times his salary," she said, before adding with a laugh, "Now, it's 30 times less," according to NRI Page.

By the time they worked together on Gautham Vasudev Menon's 2003 police drama Kaakha Kaakha, Jyotika was already an established star while Suriya was still building his career. Jyotika also revealed that she recommended Suriya's name to director Menon for the film, which became a turning point in his career, according to multiple reports.

"There is an equality in his head, and I feel you have to be born with that. It has to be an inner feel."

— Jyotika, actress

Suriya on Trust and the Karuppu Challenge

Suriya, in the same interview, expressed deep gratitude for Jyotika's support during the financial challenges surrounding his blockbuster film Karuppu. "It was a lot of financial burden. It came to me at the last minute. For me to take those extra loans, she was trusting me and allowing me to take them. Because if something goes wrong, as a family, we'd be going through it," he told The Hollywood Reporter India.

Jyotika deflected the praise: "I would not take this compliment, because this was completely his work. We do everything together. Even if it's parenting, we're always on one side of the page."

A Love Story Nearly Three Decades in the Making

Suriya and Jyotika first met on the sets of Poovellam Kettuppar in 1999, where their friendship gradually turned into romance. They grew closer while working together in films like Kaakha Kaakha and Sillunu Oru Kaadhal, becoming one of Tamil cinema's most loved on-screen pairs, according to Bollywood Life.

Their relationship initially faced opposition from Suriya's father, veteran actor Sivakumar, who later came around. "Initially, I didn't accept his love. However, he was very adamant and said that he would only live with her; otherwise, he would remain single for life," Sivakumar recalled in an interview with Galatta.

The couple married on September 11, 2006, and have two children, daughter Diya and son Dev.

Why They Haven't Acted Together Since Marriage

Despite their enduring popularity as an on-screen pair, Suriya and Jyotika have not appeared in a film together since their wedding. "I don't think we were looked at as a screen couple after marriage," Jyotika explained, according to The Hollywood Reporter India. "In the course of 25 years, there hasn't been anyone who's approached us with a film."

Both have had a remarkable year independently. Jyotika's streaming project System earned critical acclaim, while Suriya delivered the theatrical blockbuster Karuppu. At a recent promotional event for his upcoming film Vishwanath & Sons in Chennai, Suriya shared his philosophy on marriage: "Love should be everlasting. It shouldn't end once you tie the knot. You should keep loving every day, even if you've been together for 20 years," according to Zoom TV.

Their 20th wedding anniversary arrives in September 2026, with Suriya joking during the THR India interview that a professional collaboration "might have to wait until then."
